# Hatchet: Workflow Orchestration Platform Analysis

Citation-backed research evaluating Hatchet as a workflow engine for a personal
AI-assisted engineering assistant that runs CLI tools on a schedule.

## TL;DR

Hatchet is a MIT-licensed, PostgreSQL-based task queue and durable execution
engine — well-designed for code-first distributed workloads but **not a good
fit for running CLI commands on a personal workstation**. No native shell
executor (every command needs custom wrapper code), heavier deployment
footprint than n8n (6 Docker services vs 1 container), UTC-only scheduling,
and a young project (founded 2023, 7-person team, v1 in progress).

## Quick Comparison

| Dimension | Hatchet | n8n |
|-----------|---------|-----|
| License | MIT (OSI) | Sustainable Use (not OSI) |
| Self-hosting | 6 services (Docker Compose) | 1 container |
| CLI execution | Custom code per command | Execute Command node |
| Scheduling | Cron + scheduled, UTC only | Cron node, timezone support |
| API | REST + gRPC, 9 SDK clients | REST at /rest/ |
| AI/LLM | No native nodes | 70+ LangChain nodes |
| Community | 6.8k stars, 7 employees | 150k+ stars, $2.5B |
| Durable execution | Yes (event sourcing) | No |
| Idle resources | Undocumented | ~100MB |

## Stale Sheet Corrections

| Field | Sheet Said | Actually |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| License | Apache-2.0 | MIT |
| REST API | No | Yes |
| MCP Integration | Yes | Partial (monitoring only) |

## Verdict

**Not recommended for hands-on evaluation** for the PA use case. The #1
requirement (shell/CLI execution) is Hatchet's weakest dimension.
n8n remains the better fit; Temporal if durable execution is needed.

## Decision Framework

1. **Need to run CLI tools?** → n8n (Execute Command node) or Airflow (BashOperator)
2. **Need durable execution?** → Temporal or Hatchet
3. **Need MIT license?** → Hatchet (MIT) or Temporal (MIT)
4. **Need minimal footprint?** → n8n (single container, ~100MB idle)
5. **Need code-first orchestration?** → Hatchet or Temporal
